headline: Black leaders built organizations and challenged who could direct them
summary: Community organizing, a professional staff position, a board seat and a foundation presidency are different forms of authority. These examples show institution-building, mentorship and changes in representation within specific organizations.
coverageNote: Four selected episodes in community organizations and philanthropy. They do not establish a single route into all nonprofit leadership or a connection to an unresearched employer.
question: Which board minutes, appointment record or organizational history documents Black leadership at your nonprofit?

events.title: Bethune and Black women organize a national council
events.people: Mary McLeod Bethune and delegates representing Black women’s organizations
events.decisionMaker: Bethune and the participating organizations established the National Council of Negro Women
events.barrier: Bethune sought a stronger national voice for Black women on education, employment and public affairs.
events.change: She and 20 other Black women representing 14 organizations founded NCNW in New York.
events.outcome: The council developed a permanent headquarters and employed a full-time staff as its work expanded.
events.limit: Organizational leadership and staffing are documented; this account does not establish that every elected or volunteer leadership role was paid.

source.title: National Park Service · Mary McLeod Bethune
source.locator: NCNW founding, headquarters and staff paragraphs

events.title: Whitney Young mentors a future nonprofit executive
events.people: Whitney M. Young Jr. and Vernon E. Jordan Jr.
events.decisionMaker: Young offered advice and recruitment; UNCF and the National Urban League made their own executive appointments
events.barrier: Jordan’s account describes a move from southern civil-rights work into national nonprofit management.
events.change: Young recruited and advised Jordan, including encouraging him to accept leadership of the United Negro College Fund.
events.outcome: The Urban League’s chronology records Jordan as UNCF executive director in 1970 and its own leader in 1971.
events.limit: Jordan’s testimony supports a personal mentoring relationship; it does not establish that Young controlled either organization’s appointing vote or that this route served all candidates.

source.title: National Urban League · Vernon Jordan’s tribute to Whitney Young
source.locator: Jordan’s 2019 prepared remarks, recruitment and UNCF paragraphs

sources.title: National Urban League · State of Black America 2021

events.title: Black foundation professionals organize for board representation
events.people: The founding group of the Association of Black Foundation Executives
events.decisionMaker: Council on Foundations members voted on an alternative slate presented by Black professionals
events.barrier: Black foundation professionals sought greater representation in the organization governing their professional community.
events.change: At the Council on Foundations meeting, the group presented an alternative slate of Black candidates.
events.outcome: ABFE’s institutional account reports the election of five Black foundation executives to the Council’s board.
events.limit: This is a particular association’s board election, not authority to appoint executives at corporations or every nonprofit; individual ballots are not reproduced in this account.

source.title: ABFE · Its beginnings at the 1971 Council on Foundations meeting
source.locator: Paragraph describing the alternative slate and five board elections

events.title: Risa Lavizzo-Mourey takes leadership of a health foundation
events.decisionMaker: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation; the retrospective does not reproduce the appointing vote
events.barrier: RWJF had not previously been led by a woman or an African American, according to the foundation’s account.
events.change: Lavizzo-Mourey became president and chief executive officer in January 2003.
events.outcome: Her tenure included leadership of grantmaking priorities and the redesign of leadership, fellowship and scholarship programs.
events.limit: This establishes her leadership of RWJF, not a general hiring pathway for all nonprofits or proof that any particular grant created a reader’s job.

source.title: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation · Risa Lavizzo-Mourey leadership retrospective
source.locator: Opening tenure paragraphs and leadership-program discussion, September 13, 2016

furtherResearch: Find board appointment minutes, role descriptions and salary records at the reader’s organization; distinguish paid executive work from volunteer governance.
Document how Black-led organizations recruited, retained and promoted staff beyond their best-known founders.
Separate grantmaking decisions, operating revenue and the authority to select a nonprofit’s executive.
